Breadth-First Search Breadth-First Search (BFS) Breadth-First Search is an uninformed search strategy that explores the search space level by level. Breadth-First Search (BFS) It expands: • all nodes at depth 0 first • then all nodes at depth 1 • then all nodes at depth 2 • and so on Key idea: BFS always expands the shallowest unexpanded node first. ERA121 Principles of Artificial Intelligence Lecture 3: Problem Solving & Uninformed Search (Part 2) TONY HII CHANG SOON tony.hii@xmu.edu.my Cost-Based Search and Optimization Outline 1. Recap: BFS, DFS, and IDS 2. Why cost matters in search 3. Uniform Cost Search (UCS) 4. Branch and Bound (B&B) 5. UCS versus B&B Recap: Search Strategies from Last Week BFS • Complete • Optimal only when all step costs are equal • High memory usage DFS • Low memory • May find a solution quickly • Not optimal IDS • Combines the completeness of BFS with the lower memory use of DFS • Optimal when step cost is equal • Still does not consider different path costs Why BFS, DFS & IDS are still not enough • BFS, DFS, and IDS mainly focus on the structure or depth of the search tree. • They do not handle unequal path costs properly. • In many real applications, the cheapest solution is not the shallowest one. • Therefore, we need search methods that consider cost. Two cost-based needs in AI search • In some problems, we want the least-cost path from a start node to a goal node. • In other problems, we want the optimal solution among many possible complete solutions. • These two needs lead to two different methods: ❖ Uniform Cost Search (UCS) ❖ Branch and Bound (B&B) Uniform Cost Search Uniform Cost Search (UCS) • Uniform Cost Search is an uninformed search algorithm. • It expands the node on the frontier with the lowest path cost from the start state. • It uses the evaluation function: 𝑓 𝑛 = 𝑔(𝑛) Where: 𝑔(𝑛) = actual cost from the start state to node n Main idea of UCS • Start from the initial node with cost 0. • Put the node into a priority queue. • Always remove the node with the smallest cumulative cost. • Expand its neighbors and update their costs. • Repeat until the goal node is selected. How UCS works? 1. Insert the start node into OPEN with g=0. 2. Remove the node with the smallest g(n) from OPEN. 3. If it is the goal node, stop. 4. Otherwise, expand its neighbors. 5.
